chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: The drugstore job and the bicycle he had to pay for
summary: Cobb gets a bicycle for a $7-a-week drugstore job, eats free ice cream, and finds it deducted from his first pay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x:
But I had buddies; I had 2 buddies that went to work in the evenings. It was my first project, and I said, "Gee willikers, I got to get me a job, too" -- so first thing I did, I asked my mother to get me a bicycle; I could get a job working at the drugstore working in the evenings. And she consented. Anything I asked for, she'd do.

So she got me a bicycle -- $20 she had to pay for it.
In those days ... I had a job secured [Schuller's] already at Schulle Pharmacy just 3 blocks from my house, and I started at 4 o'clock in the evening, and worked till closing time, making $7 a week.

And now, she bought the bicycle and she wouldn't let me go downtown and pick it up. She got a big friend of hers in the next block, AND on a Saturday, and she worked Saturdays only a half a day, and she was out to work and I was standing on the sidewalk there, and when he brought that

bicycle, I snatched it out from under him. "It's mine!" He wanted to bring it to me, he had gone out and picked it up for me, but I wanted to let him know that it was mine. "Let me have it." I'm a kid, now. And when I got that bicycle on Saturday, I won't walked to Schuller's on Sunday and told them I'd be ready to start Monday -- and I did start Monday.
My first week, working with all that ice cream, he said, "Go back and get what you want." I didn't know he was clockin' it takin' gonna take it and deduct it from my salary!

My first week's salary was slips, and my mother told me I wasn't going to pay for that bicycle if I didn't pay her back. I took her the slips, and she said, "This will never do." I paid $20 hard earned money, and I borrowed it." Oh, I felt so bad. But you know, that man was smart. "Go on and get whatever you want!" But everything you get took, he'd write it down.
Next week, I came on with full salary. I didn't get nothing -- I didn't need no ice-cream because I'm gonna face my mother.
Well, you know, in some jobs like that, they let you eat as much as you want, so that you're sick of it.
I say that some jobs spread their
ice cream and candies -- and the kids that work there, they let them eat as much as they like, but after about a week, they're sick of it, because they've eaten so much.
I got sick of it the first week, when I got reprimanded by my mother. That's when I got sick of it.
